newsitem.title: USA: Opta Food to distribute konjac ingredient.
newsitem.headline: Opta Food to distribute konjac ingredient.

text.p: Opta Food Ingredients Inc said it had signed a letter of intent and entered negotiations to become the exclusive U.S. distributor of the food ingredient konjac flour for Shimizu Chemical Corp of Japan.

The agreement, which provides Opta the right for the sale of konjac in food products, will begin in January 1998. The company said it did not expect the agreement to affect its 1997 revenue and that it was too early to evaluate its impact for 1998.
Konjac flour is a versatile hydrocolloid obtained from the konjac plant commonly cultivated in east Asia. Chemically, it is a polysaccharide made of glucose and mannose sugars.

It is used in Asia to prepare traditional foods, such as heat stable noodles, known as konnyaku. Konjac flour has been used in the United States since at least the turn of the century, most recently as a thickening or gelling agent in processed foods.
